correctness.rationale: The sigma/n monotonicity proof excludes support <=4 and forces the 5-prime form 3*5*7*r*s. Exact abundance yields r in {11,13,17,19} and four finite s bounds, producing 87 prime pairs. The elementary congruence obstruction reduces these to 45. Every odd squarefree non-square n has 16 disjoint complementary divisor pairs; the subset-sum characterization of sigma(n)-2n is necessary and sufficient. Two different exact programs exhaust all 45, with no solutions. Six different primes multiply to 937365 and five displayed omitted complementary pairs sum to sigma(n)-2n=60630, giving an explicit representation. Both actual submitted files were executed; no infinite theorem is inferred from numerical experiments.

originality.rationale: The claim establishes an unrestricted odd squarefree five-prime impossibility, not only an observed six-prime example. Six exact-topic searches found no record covering the five-prime range. The motivating 2026 preprint provides a squarefree six-prime witness and some modular/excess restrictions, but its implication reaches neither all 45 abundance-admissible five-prime cases nor the proved support minimum. The earlier general paper and the integer-sequence table do not furnish that exclusion; a closest published three-prime lower-support result and an even two-prime family likewise cannot imply it. Possibility of an unindexed older exhaustive tabulation remains.
residual_risks: An earlier unindexed exact computation or an implicit finite reduction may have proved the same support minimum.
Full text of the closest published three-factor result was not accessible; its public summary covers a strictly smaller support range.
The scientific review is not an independent audit.

value.rationale: The minimum distinct-prime support of an odd squarefree strongly pseudoperfect number is a canonical invariant of a natural class. The recent primary paper points to odd primitive examples and explicitly exhibits a six-prime squarefree witness but does not settle whether five suffice. This theorem gives an exact sharp obstruction for the entire five-prime stratum, improving understanding of the boundary between abundance and a complementation-closed divisor subset. The finite work is substantive because abundance and congruence make the unrestricted classification provably finite and two independent exhaustive checks close it.
